topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture series and establishes the learning goals for this lecture.

topics.label: Cellular changes, differentiation and tissue organization in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain cancer as an acquired disruption of normal cellular differentiation and tissue organization that experimental models must capture.

topics.label: Distinguishing benign and malignant tumors through invasion and metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how tumor spread distinguishes malignant behavior from benign growth and how that distinction is recognized in tissues.

topics.label: Benign tumors: malignant progression and potential harm
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the clinical potential of benign tumors, showing that progression to malignancy is possible but neither inevitable nor necessary for serious harm.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumor names indicate tissue of origin and malignant status, including exceptions to the naming rules.

topics.label: How cancer causes illness and death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumor growth disrupts normal bodily function and produces potentially fatal disease.

topics.label: Tumor incidence in humans and other animals
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare the occurrence of tumor types across populations and species.

topics.label: Clinical detection and cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain why early cancer detection is needed and what determines the effectiveness of screening for different tumors.

topics.label: Lecture close and revision guidance
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by returning to the learning outcomes and directing students toward revision and upcoming practicals.
